name: Arlo Arc Floor Lamp

The smoked-glass dome throws a warm, pooled light rather than a glare, so it reads like a 1960s den after dark. Suits a mid-century living room that needs overhead light without the ceiling work.

Shade: smoked glass dome, 12 in diameter
Dimensions: 78 in H x 54 in reach x 12 in base diameter
Base: cast iron with walnut veneer cap, 28 lb
Cord: 8 ft fabric-wrapped cord with inline foot dimmer
Wipe with a dry cloth; assembled in Portugal

name: Haldane Tripod Floor Lamp
description: Three tapered legs of pale solid ash hold a wide, soft-white linen drum at reading height. The light is quiet and diffuse, the kind that makes a pale, uncluttered room feel calm at night. Light enough to carry from the sofa to the bedroom, it suits small apartments and airy, light-filled rooms.

name: Foundry Floor Lamp
description: A blackened-steel column on a block of reclaimed oak, topped with a swiveling spun-metal shade and visible knurled hardware. It has the raw, utilitarian look of a workshop task light and throws a focused beam wherever you aim it. Made for a loft, a studio desk, or anyone who likes their lighting exposed rather than dressed up.

name: Sable Paper Floor Lamp
description: A tall, narrow column of hand-folded washi paper on a slim black-stained oak frame, with the paper left slightly uneven so each one is a little different. It glows rather than shines, filling a corner with a soft, even light that makes a spare room feel settled. For a calm bedroom or a low, quiet living room with very little else in it.

description: A fluted brass column rises from a disc of honed Carrara marble to a wide pleated shade in deep emerald velvet. Every detail is polished and geometric, and the shade turns the light a rich, flattering gold once evening sets in. A glamorous anchor for a formal living room or a bedroom that leans into jewel tones.

It looks like something picked up on a trip and lived with for years, relaxed and textured, and it pairs easily with jute, plants and layered cottons. For a sideboard, a bedside, or a sunny reading spot.

Pairs well with pine, wool throws and a stack of well-read books.
